fr.B: Voici les proverbes de Salomon, fils de David, roi d’Israël.
fr.R: Voici de sages paroles de Salomon, le fils de David. Salomon était roi d’Israël.

sw.R: Haya ni maneno ya hekima ya Sulemani, mwana wa Daudi. Sulemani alikuwa mfalme wa Israeli.

es.R: Estos son dichos sabios de Salomón, el hijo de David. Salomón era rey de Israel.

vi.L: Châm ngôn của Sa-lô-môn, con trai Đa-vít, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Đây là những châm ngôn của Sa-lô-môn, con trai Đa-vít, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Đây là những lời khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn, con trai của Đa-vít. Sa-lô-môn là vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 다윗의 아들, 이스라엘의 왕 솔로몬의 잠언.
ko.B: 이것은 다윗의 아들이며 이스라엘의 왕인 솔로몬의 잠언이다.
ko.R: 이것은 다윗의 아들 솔로몬이 남긴 지혜로운 말들이다. 솔로몬은 이스라엘의 왕이었다.

decisions.choice: proverbs: short, memorable sayings that teach by comparison
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) covers short sayings (10:1), longer teaching poems (chapters 1–9), comparisons and even taunts (Isaiah 14:4). Its root is linked with being "like", and many proverbs teach by setting two things side by side.

decisions.choice: the proverbs of Solomon: a title for the book as a whole
decisions.reason: The title names Solomon, whose wisdom and three thousand proverbs are recorded in 1 Kings 4:29–34. The book itself also gathers "words of the wise" (22:17; 24:23), proverbs of Solomon copied by the men of Hezekiah (25:1), and the words of Agur (30:1) and of King Lemuel (31:1).

decisions.choice: wise sayings
decisions.reason: "Proverbs" may be an unfamiliar word for young readers; Readable says what they are.

decisions.choice: the father's teaching and the sayings are speech, in the present and future of speech at every level; the reader is addressed with "tu"
decisions.reason: Proverbs is not narrative, so the passé simple of French narrative has no place in it. The father speaks to one son, so French uses "tu", as it does to one person throughout this translation.

decisions.choice: "mithali" for the proverbs of the title (L, B); "maneno ya hekima" at Readable, as the English Readable explains the word
decisions.reason: "Methali" is the everyday Swahili word for a proverb; "mithali" is the form long used for this book and for weighty sayings, and keeps the title recognisable. Readable says what the sayings are.

decisions.choice: dichos sabios
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, "proverbios" is explained for young readers as short wise sayings.

decisions.choice: "châm ngôn" (L, B); "những lời khôn ngoan" (R)
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) names short sayings that teach. "châm ngôn" is the usual Vietnamese word for such sayings and for this book; "tục ngữ" means folk sayings with no author. Readable says what they are, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "잠언" (L, B); "지혜로운 말" (R)
decisions.reason: "잠언" is the Korean name of the book and of this kind of saying (meaning decision m1). Readable says plainly what the word is, as the English Readable does with "wise sayings"; "속담" would suggest folk sayings of unknown origin.

source.text: לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֣ה וּמוּסָ֑ר לְ֝הָבִ֗ין אִמְרֵ֥י בִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For knowing wisdom and discipline, for understanding sayings of understanding,

en.L: For knowing wisdom and discipline, \q for understanding sayings of understanding,
en.B: They are for learning wisdom and discipline, \q for grasping words of insight,
en.R: They will help you become wise and learn from correction. \q They will help you understand words that make things clear.

fr.L: Pour connaître la sagesse et la discipline, \q pour comprendre les paroles d’intelligence,
fr.B: Ils servent à acquérir la sagesse et la discipline, \q à saisir les paroles pleines d’intelligence,
fr.R: Ils t’aideront à devenir sage et à profiter de la correction. \q Ils t’aideront à comprendre des paroles qui éclairent.

sw.L: Kwa kujua hekima na nidhamu, \q kwa kufahamu maneno ya ufahamu,
sw.B: Ni kwa ajili ya kujifunza hekima na nidhamu, \q kwa ajili ya kuelewa maneno ya busara,
sw.R: Zitakusaidia kuwa na hekima na kujifunza kutokana na maonyo. \q Zitakusaidia kuelewa maneno yanayoweka mambo wazi.

es.L: Para conocer sabiduría y disciplina, \q para entender dichos de entendimiento,
es.B: Sirven para aprender sabiduría y disciplina, \q para captar palabras de inteligencia,
es.R: Te ayudarán a ser sabio y a aprender de la corrección. \q Te ayudarán a entender palabras que aclaran las cosas.

vi.L: Để biết sự khôn ngoan và sự sửa dạy, \q để hiểu những lời của sự thông sáng,
vi.B: Các châm ngôn này giúp người ta học biết sự khôn ngoan và sự sửa dạy, \q hiểu thấu những lời thông sáng,
vi.R: Những lời này giúp bạn trở nên khôn ngoan và học được từ sự sửa dạy. \q Chúng giúp bạn hiểu những lời làm cho mọi điều sáng tỏ.

ko.L: 지혜와 훈계를 알기 위한 것, \q 명철의 말들을 깨닫기 위한 것,
ko.B: 이 잠언은 지혜와 훈계를 배우게 하고, \q 명철의 말을 깨닫게 하려는 것이며,
ko.R: 이 말들은 사람을 지혜롭게 하고 훈계를 받아 배우게 해 준다. \q 일을 밝히 보여 주는 말을 깨닫게 해 준다.

decisions.choice: wisdom: skill in living well
decisions.reason: The word (hokmah) is used for a craftsman's skill (Exodus 31:3, 6) as well as for good judgment. In Proverbs it is the skill of living rightly before God and with other people, not book learning.

decisions.choice: discipline: instruction that corrects
decisions.reason: The word (musar) means training that corrects, whether by words (1:8) or by the rod (22:15). It runs through Proverbs alongside wisdom (1:3, 7, 8).

decisions.choice: for knowing ... for understanding: the purpose of the book
decisions.reason: Verses 2–6 are a chain of phrases saying what the proverbs named in verse 1 are for. The Hebrew plays on one root: "to understand words of understanding".

decisions.choice: They are for (B); They will help you (R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew strings the purpose phrases onto the title. Balanced and Readable supply a subject so that the sentence stands on its own.

decisions.choice: "la sagesse", "l'intelligence" and "la discipline" (Literal, Balanced), "la correction" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: These are the book's key words and keep one French word each. Musar is teaching that corrects; "discipline" keeps both sides at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says plainly "la correction".

decisions.choice: "hekima" for wisdom at every level; "nidhamu" for discipline (L, B) and "maonyo" (correction) at Readable, for the whole of Proverbs
decisions.reason: "Nidhamu" is training that keeps a person in line, close to the Hebrew musar; Readable uses "maonyo", the warnings and corrections a parent gives, which young readers know well.

decisions.choice: disciplina (L, B); corrección (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (musar) is training that corrects. Literal and Balanced say "disciplina" throughout Proverbs; Readable says "corrección", the plainer word for what a parent does. "Enseñanza" is kept for the parent's teaching (torah).

decisions.choice: "sự khôn ngoan" for wisdom and "sự sửa dạy" for discipline, at every level and through the book
decisions.reason: Wisdom here is skill in living well, and the second word is instruction that corrects (see the meaning decisions). "sự sửa dạy" keeps both teaching and correcting together; "kỷ luật" sounds like rules and punishment, "giáo huấn" like a lecture.

decisions.choice: "bạn" for the reader the book addresses in 1:2-6
decisions.reason: The opening verses speak of the book's purpose to anyone who reads it, before the father starts speaking to his son in verse 8. "bạn" is the neutral modern word for a reader of any age.

decisions.choice: "지혜" for ḥokmah and "훈계" for musar at every level; "명철" (L, B) and "깨달음" or a plain verb (R) for binah
decisions.reason: These are the key words of Proverbs, and the same Korean word is kept for each wherever it comes back, so the reader hears the book's repetitions. "훈계" is instruction that corrects (meaning decision m2); "징계" leans toward punishment. Readable uses plainer native words for understanding. This holds for chapters 1-11.

source.text: לָ֭קַחַת מוּסַ֣ר הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל צֶ֥דֶק וּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט וּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For receiving discipline of insight, righteousness and justice and uprightness,

en.L: for receiving the discipline of insight, \q righteousness and justice and uprightness,
en.B: for taking in the training that brings good sense: \q righteousness, justice and fairness,
en.R: They will teach you to live with good sense, \q and to do what is right, fair and honest.

fr.L: pour recevoir la discipline du bon sens, \q la justice, le droit et la droiture,
fr.B: pour recevoir la formation qui donne du bon sens : \q la justice, le droit et l’équité,
fr.R: Ils t’apprendront à vivre avec bon sens, \q et à faire ce qui est juste, équitable et honnête.

sw.L: kwa kupokea nidhamu ya busara, \q haki na uadilifu na unyofu,
sw.B: kwa kupokea mafunzo yaletayo busara: \q haki, uadilifu na usawa,
sw.R: Zitakufundisha kuishi kwa busara, \q na kutenda yaliyo mema, ya haki na ya uaminifu.

es.L: para recibir la disciplina del buen juicio, \q justicia y derecho y rectitud,
es.B: para acoger la formación que da buen juicio: \q justicia, derecho y equidad,
es.R: Te enseñarán a vivir con buen juicio \q y a hacer lo que es justo, recto y honrado.

vi.L: để nhận lấy sự sửa dạy của sự sáng suốt, \q sự công chính, công lý và sự ngay thẳng,
vi.B: để tiếp nhận sự sửa dạy giúp mình biết suy xét: \q sự công chính, công lý và công bằng,
vi.R: Chúng dạy bạn sống biết suy xét, \q và làm điều đúng, điều công bằng và ngay thẳng.

ko.L: 통찰의 훈계를 받기 위한 것, \q 의와 공의와 정직을 [위한 것],
ko.B: 분별 있게 살도록 이끄는 훈계를 받아들여 \q 의롭고 공정하고 공평하게 하려는 것이며,
ko.R: 이 말들은 훈계를 받아 분별 있게 살도록 가르쳐 준다. \q 옳고 공정하고 정직하게 살도록 가르쳐 준다.

decisions.choice: discipline of insight: training that makes a person act with good sense
decisions.reason: The word (haskel) is a verb form, "acting wisely" or "having insight". Here it names what the training produces: a person who sees what to do and does it.

decisions.choice: righteousness, justice and uprightness: right dealing with others
decisions.reason: The three words often go together (2:9). Righteousness (tsedeq) is doing what is right by God and neighbor; justice (mishpat) is fair judgment; uprightness is straight, honest dealing.

decisions.choice: what is right, fair and honest
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three nouns into plain adjectives with the same meaning.

source.text: לָתֵ֣ת לִפְתָאיִ֣ם עָרְמָ֑ה לְ֝נַ֗עַר דַּ֣עַת וּמְזִמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For giving to simple ones prudence, to a youth knowledge and discretion.

en.L: for giving prudence to [the] simple, \q to [the] young knowledge and discretion.
en.B: for making the naive shrewd, \q and giving the young knowledge and the ability to plan wisely.
en.R: They give good sense to people who are easily fooled. \q They give young people knowledge and help them plan well.

fr.L: pour donner aux simples la prudence, \q au jeune la connaissance et la réflexion.
fr.B: pour rendre avisés les naïfs \q et donner aux jeunes la connaissance et l’art de bien réfléchir.
fr.R: Ils donnent du bon sens à ceux qui se laissent tromper. \q Ils donnent aux jeunes la connaissance et les aident à bien prévoir.

sw.L: kwa kuwapa wajinga werevu, \q kijana maarifa na uwezo wa kupanga.
sw.B: ili kuwafanya wajinga wawe werevu, \q na kuwapa vijana maarifa na uwezo wa kupanga kwa hekima.
sw.R: Zinawapa busara watu wanaodanganywa kwa urahisi. \q Zinawapa vijana maarifa na kuwasaidia kupanga vizuri.

es.L: para dar prudencia a [los] simples, \q [al] joven conocimiento y discreción.
es.B: para volver astutos a los ingenuos \q y dar a los jóvenes conocimiento y capacidad de planear con sabiduría.
es.R: Dan buen juicio a los que se dejan engañar. \q Dan a los jóvenes conocimiento y los ayudan a planear bien.

vi.L: để ban sự khôn khéo cho người khờ dại, \q cho người trẻ tri thức và sự thận trọng.
vi.B: để làm cho người khờ dại trở nên khôn khéo, \q và ban cho người trẻ tri thức cùng khả năng tính toán khôn ngoan.
vi.R: Chúng giúp người dễ bị lừa biết suy xét. \q Chúng ban tri thức cho người trẻ và giúp họ biết tính toán cho tốt.

ko.L: 어리석은 자들에게 슬기를, \q 젊은이에게 지식과 분별을 주기 위한 것이다.
ko.B: 순진한 사람을 슬기롭게 하고, \q 젊은이에게 지식과 바르게 계획하는 힘을 주려는 것이다.
ko.R: 이 말들은 쉽게 속는 사람에게 분별력을 준다. \q 젊은이에게 지식을 주고 일을 잘 계획하도록 돕는다.

decisions.choice: simple: naive, easily led
decisions.reason: The simple (petayim) are people not yet formed, who believe whatever they hear (14:15). They are not yet set in folly, so wisdom speaks to them (1:22; 9:4). The root may mean "open", easy to persuade (compare 1:10).

decisions.choice: prudence ... discretion: shrewdness and the power to plan
decisions.reason: Both words can be used of bad cunning (the serpent is "crafty" in Genesis 3:1, the same root as prudence; schemes in 12:2). Here they are good: the shrewdness that sees through a trap, and the ability to think ahead.

decisions.choice: naive
decisions.reason: "Simple" in modern English suggests low intelligence. The Hebrew word means inexperienced and gullible, which "naive" says. Literal keeps "simple".

decisions.choice: "les simples" (Literal), "les naïfs" (Balanced), "ceux qui se laissent tromper" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The word describes people who are open to every influence, not stupid people. "Les simples" is the traditional word but today can sound like "simple-minded"; Balanced says "naïfs", and Readable says what such people are like.

decisions.choice: "wajinga" for the simple (L, B); "watu wanaodanganywa kwa urahisi" (people easily deceived) at Readable, for the whole book
decisions.reason: "Mjinga" here means a naive person who has not yet learned, not someone stupid; Readable spells out what the word means, since many readers hear "mjinga" as an insult.

decisions.choice: los simples (L); los ingenuos (B); los que se dejan engañar (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (peti) is someone open to every influence, not yet set in folly. Literal keeps the old word "simples"; Balanced says "ingenuos"; Readable says what such people are like. These forms are kept throughout Proverbs.

decisions.choice: "người khờ dại" (L, B); "người dễ bị lừa" (R)
decisions.reason: The simple person is naive and easily led, not stupid (see the meaning decision). "khờ dại" says that plainly; "đơn sơ" can sound like praise. Readable says what such a person is like.

decisions.choice: "tri thức" for knowledge (L, B), "sự thông sáng" for understanding (1:2)
decisions.reason: Proverbs keeps knowledge and understanding as two words in a pair, so Literal and Balanced keep two Vietnamese words for them; Readable may say "sự hiểu biết" for either.

decisions.choice: "어리석은 자" (L), "순진한 사람" (B), "쉽게 속는 사람" (R) for peti
decisions.reason: The peti is not wicked but naive and easily led (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the traditional word, Balanced says naive, Readable says what the person is like. "미련한 자" is kept for the fool (kesil, ʾewil), a different word. This holds for chapters 1-11.

source.text: יִשְׁמַ֣ע חָ֭כָם וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶ֑קַח וְ֝נָב֗וֹן תַּחְבֻּל֥וֹת יִקְנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Let hear [the] wise and let him increase learning, and [the] discerning, guidance let him acquire,

en.L: Let [the] wise hear and increase learning, \q and let [the] discerning acquire guidance,
en.B: Let the wise listen and gain still more learning; \q let those with understanding acquire skill to steer their way,
en.R: Wise people should listen to them and learn even more. \q People with understanding should get good advice from them.

fr.L: Que le sage écoute et accroisse [son] savoir, \q et que celui qui discerne acquière l’art de se diriger,
fr.B: Que le sage écoute et apprenne encore davantage ; \q que celui qui a de l’intelligence acquière l’art de bien se conduire,
fr.R: Les sages doivent les écouter et apprendre encore plus. \q Ceux qui ont de l’intelligence y trouveront de bons conseils.

sw.L: Mwenye hekima na asikie na aongeze elimu, \q na mwenye ufahamu apate maongozi,
sw.B: Mwenye hekima na asikilize, apate kuongeza elimu; \q mwenye ufahamu apate ustadi wa kuongoza njia yake,
sw.R: Watu wenye hekima wanapaswa kusikiliza na kujifunza zaidi. \q Watu wenye ufahamu wanapaswa kupata mashauri mema kutoka katika mithali hizi.

es.L: Que oiga [el] sabio y aumente su saber, \q y [el] entendido adquiera dirección,
es.B: Que el sabio escuche y aumente aún más su saber; \q que el entendido adquiera destreza para guiar su camino,
es.R: Las personas sabias deben escucharlos y aprender todavía más. \q Las personas con entendimiento deben recibir de ellos buenos consejos.

vi.L: Người khôn ngoan hãy nghe và thêm sự học hỏi, \q và người thông sáng hãy thu lấy sự hướng dẫn,
vi.B: Người khôn ngoan hãy lắng nghe để học thêm nữa; \q người hiểu biết hãy học lấy tài lèo lái đường đi,
vi.R: Người khôn ngoan nên nghe những lời này để học thêm. \q Người hiểu biết nên nhận lấy lời khuyên tốt từ đó.

ko.L: 지혜로운 자는 듣고 배움을 더하라. \q 명철한 자는 지략을 얻으라.
ko.B: 지혜로운 사람은 듣고 더 배우며, \q 명철한 사람은 바르게 길을 잡아 가는 솜씨를 얻어라.
ko.R: 지혜로운 사람도 이 말을 듣고 더 배워야 한다. \q 깨달음이 있는 사람도 여기에서 좋은 조언을 얻어야 한다.

decisions.choice: let the wise hear: an invitation inside the list
decisions.reason: The verbs may be read as wishes ("let him hear") or as plain futures ("the wise will hear"). Either way the verse breaks into the list of purposes to say that the proverbs are not only for beginners.

decisions.choice: guidance: skill in steering
decisions.reason: The word (tahbulot) is related to the word for a ship's rope and its sailor (Ezekiel 27:8), so it pictures steering. It is the skill of finding a course through life (11:14; 24:6).

decisions.choice: skill to steer their way
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of steering that the Hebrew word carries (m2).

decisions.choice: "mwenye ufahamu" for the discerning; "ufahamu" (L, B, R) and "busara" for binah and tevunah through the book
decisions.reason: "Ufahamu" is understanding that sees into things; "busara" is good sense in acting. Keeping these two words for the Hebrew pair lets readers follow the book's key terms.

source.text: לְהָבִ֣ין מָ֭שָׁל וּמְלִיצָ֑ה דִּבְרֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים וְחִידֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: To understand a proverb and a figure, words of wise ones and their riddles.

en.L: to understand a proverb and a figure, \q the words of the wise and their riddles.
en.B: so that they understand proverbs and figures of speech, \q the sayings of the wise and their riddles.
en.R: Then they will understand proverbs and word pictures, \q and the sayings and riddles of wise people.

fr.L: pour comprendre un proverbe et une figure, \q les paroles des sages et leurs énigmes.
fr.B: afin de comprendre les proverbes et les paroles imagées, \q les paroles des sages et leurs énigmes.
fr.R: Alors ils comprendront les proverbes et les images, \q les paroles et les énigmes des sages.

sw.L: ili kufahamu mithali na fumbo, \q maneno ya wenye hekima na mafumbo yao.
sw.B: ili waelewe mithali na misemo ya picha, \q maneno ya wenye hekima na mafumbo yao.
sw.R: Ndipo watakapoelewa mithali na maneno ya mifano, \q na maneno na mafumbo ya watu wenye hekima.

es.L: para entender proverbio y figura, \q las palabras de los sabios y sus enigmas.
es.B: para que entiendan proverbios y figuras, \q los dichos de los sabios y sus enigmas.
es.R: Así entenderán los proverbios y las comparaciones, \q y los dichos y adivinanzas de los sabios.

vi.L: để hiểu châm ngôn và ẩn dụ, \q lời của những người khôn ngoan và những câu đố của họ.
vi.B: để hiểu các châm ngôn và lời ví von, \q những lời của người khôn ngoan và các câu đố của họ.
vi.R: Rồi họ sẽ hiểu các châm ngôn và những lời ví von, \q cùng những câu nói và câu đố của người khôn ngoan.

ko.L: 잠언과 비유를, \q 지혜로운 자들의 말과 그들의 수수께끼를 깨닫기 위한 것이다.
ko.B: 잠언과 비유, \q 지혜로운 이들의 말과 그 수수께끼를 깨닫게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 그러면 잠언과 그림 같은 말, \q 지혜로운 사람들의 말과 수수께끼를 알아듣게 된다.

decisions.choice: figure ... riddles: sayings whose meaning must be worked out
decisions.reason: A figure (melitsah) is a saying that needs interpreting (Habakkuk 2:6). A riddle (hidah) is a puzzling saying, like Samson's (Judges 14:12) or the hard questions the queen of Sheba brought to Solomon (1 Kings 10:1).

decisions.choice: to understand: continuing verse 5
decisions.reason: The phrase may carry on the list in verses 2–4 or say what the guidance of verse 5 leads to. The sense is the same: the proverbs train readers to understand wise sayings.

source.text: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה רֵאשִׁ֣ית דָּ֑עַת חָכְמָ֥ה וּ֝מוּסָ֗ר אֱוִילִ֥ים בָּֽזוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [is the] beginning of knowledge; wisdom and discipline fools despise.

en.L: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] the beginning of knowledge; \q wisdom and discipline fools despise.
en.B: Knowledge begins with the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but fools treat wisdom and discipline with contempt.
en.R: Real knowledge starts with honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe. \q Fools look down on wisdom and correction.

fr.L: La crainte {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [est] le commencement de la connaissance ; \q la sagesse et la discipline, les insensés [les] méprisent.
fr.B: La connaissance commence par la crainte {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q mais les insensés méprisent la sagesse et la discipline.
fr.R: La vraie connaissance commence quand on honore {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avec respect. \q Les insensés méprisent la sagesse et la correction.

sw.L: Kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] mwanzo wa maarifa; \q hekima na nidhamu wapumbavu huzidharau.
sw.B: Maarifa huanza kwa kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q lakini wapumbavu huidharau hekima na nidhamu.
sw.R: Maarifa ya kweli huanza kwa kumheshimu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa hofu takatifu. \q Wapumbavu huidharau hekima na maonyo.

es.L: El temor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [es] el principio del conocimiento; \q la sabiduría y la disciplina desprecian los necios.
es.B: El conocimiento comienza con el temor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q pero los necios desprecian la sabiduría y la disciplina.
es.R: El verdadero conocimiento empieza por honrar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} con reverencia. \q Los necios menosprecian la sabiduría y la corrección.

vi.L: Sự kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [là] khởi đầu của tri thức; \q sự khôn ngoan và sự sửa dạy, kẻ ngu dại khinh thường.
vi.B: Tri thức bắt đầu từ sự kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q nhưng kẻ ngu dại xem thường sự khôn ngoan và sự sửa dạy.
vi.R: Hiểu biết thật bắt đầu từ việc tôn kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Người ngu dại coi khinh sự khôn ngoan và lời sửa dạy.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외함이 지식의 시작이다. \q 지혜와 훈계를 미련한 자들은 업신여긴다.
ko.B: 지식은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외함에서 시작된다. \q 그러나 미련한 자들은 지혜와 훈계를 업신여긴다.
ko.R: 참된 지식은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 두려운 마음으로 섬기는 데서 시작된다. \q 미련한 사람은 지혜와 훈계를 우습게 여긴다.

decisions.choice: the fear of the LORD: reverent awe that trusts and obeys
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is the motto of the book (9:10; 15:33) and of its last chapter (31:30). It is not dread that runs from God but awe that turns from evil (3:7; 8:13) and trusts him (14:26).

decisions.choice: beginning: the starting point, and also the chief part
decisions.reason: The word (reshit) can mean the first of something (Genesis 1:1) or the best of it (Amos 6:6). Proverbs 9:10 says the same thing with a word that means only "beginning", so the starting point is the main sense: knowledge does not begin anywhere else.

decisions.choice: fools: people who reject correction
decisions.reason: The fool here (evil) is not slow-witted but morally stubborn: he despises discipline (15:5) and cannot keep quiet (10:14). The Hebrew puts "wisdom and discipline" first, before "fools despise", for emphasis.

decisions.choice: Knowledge begins with
alternatives: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the sentence in an order that sounds natural in English while keeping each word; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: honoring ... with awe
decisions.reason: In modern English "fear" alone suggests being afraid. Readable says what the fear of the LORD is (m1).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals for the divine name, with "Yahvé" as the reader's alternative, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch: capitals mark the name, as the English "the LORD" does. "L'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: "la crainte du SEIGNEUR" (Literal, Balanced); "honorer le SEIGNEUR avec respect" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The phrase means reverent awe that trusts and obeys (meaning decision m1), not fear of punishment. Literal and Balanced keep the traditional phrase; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "kumcha BWANA" (L, B); "kumheshimu BWANA kwa hofu takatifu" at Readable, wherever the fear of the LORD comes in Proverbs
decisions.reason: "Kumcha" is the Swahili verb for reverent fear of God, not plain fright; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "BWANA" in capitals by default, "Yahwe" as the setting alternative
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Old Testament: the capitals show that the Hebrew has the divine name here, and the reader may switch to the name itself.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: God's name YHWH is "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, as in the rest of the Spanish Old Testament, with "Yahvé" as the reader's alternative. The span takes in the article and its contraction (del SEÑOR, al SEÑOR).

decisions.choice: honrar al SEÑOR con reverencia
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, "temor" could sound like plain fright; Readable says it is honoring the LORD with awe. Literal and Balanced keep "el temor del SEÑOR" throughout Proverbs.

decisions.choice: "sự kính sợ CHÚA" (L, B); "tôn kính CHÚA" (R); the name as "CHÚA" with "Gia-vê" as the setting's alternative
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is reverent awe that trusts and obeys (see the meaning decision). "kính sợ" holds both respect and fear; Readable says "tôn kính" (honor with reverence), as the English Readable does. The capitals mark the name YHWH, as in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: "kẻ ngu dại" (L, B); "người ngu dại" (R)
decisions.reason: One word for the fool through the book. "kẻ" keeps the disapproval the Hebrew has; Readable uses the plainer "người".

decisions.choice: YHWH is {{divine_name:주|야훼}} at every level, with the particle outside the span
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 7a): "주" (Lord) by default, the name "야훼" as the alternative, as the English has "the LORD|Yahweh". "여호와", the form of the older Protestant Bibles, is not used. Both forms end in a vowel, so one particle fits both. This holds for chapters 1-11.

decisions.choice: "주를 경외함" (L, B) and "주를 두려운 마음으로 섬김" (R) for the fear of the LORD; "미련한 자" (L, B), "미련한 사람" (R) for the fool
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is reverent awe that trusts and obeys (meaning decision m1), not terror; "경외" says awe, and Readable spells it out in plain words. The fool (ʾewil) is the one who rejects correction (m3); "어리석은 자" is kept for the naive (peti), a different word. These hold for chapters 1-11.

source.text: שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי מוּסַ֣ר אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝טֹּ֗שׁ תּוֹרַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, my son, [the] discipline of your father, and do not forsake [the] teaching of your mother.

en.L: Hear, my son, the discipline of your father, \q and do not let go [of] the teaching of your mother.
en.B: My son, listen when your father corrects you, \q and do not let go of what your mother teaches you.
en.R: My son, listen when your father corrects you. \q Do not turn away from what your mother teaches you.

fr.L: Écoute, mon fils, la discipline de ton père, \q et ne délaisse pas l’enseignement de ta mère.
fr.B: Mon fils, écoute ton père quand il te corrige, \q et ne laisse pas de côté ce que ta mère t’enseigne.
fr.R: Mon fils, écoute ton père quand il te corrige. \q Ne te détourne pas de ce que ta mère t’apprend.

sw.L: Sikia, mwanangu, nidhamu ya baba yako, \q wala usiyaache mafundisho ya mama yako.
sw.B: Mwanangu, sikiliza baba yako anapokuonya, \q wala usiyaache mafundisho ya mama yako.
sw.R: Mwanangu, msikilize baba yako anapokuonya. \q Usiache kufuata yale ambayo mama yako anakufundisha.

es.L: Escucha, hijo mío, la disciplina de tu padre, \q y no abandones la enseñanza de tu madre.
es.B: Hijo mío, escucha cuando tu padre te corrige, \q y no dejes lo que tu madre te enseña.
es.R: Hijo mío, escucha cuando tu padre te corrige. \q No te apartes de lo que tu madre te enseña.

vi.L: Hỡi con ta, hãy nghe sự sửa dạy của cha con, \q và đừng bỏ lời dạy của mẹ con.
vi.B: Con ơi, hãy nghe khi cha sửa dạy con, \q và đừng buông bỏ lời mẹ dạy con.
vi.R: Con ơi, hãy lắng nghe khi cha sửa dạy con. \q Đừng quay lưng với những điều mẹ dạy con.

ko.L: 들어라, 내 아들아, 네 아버지의 훈계를. \q 그리고 네 어머니의 가르침을 버리지 마라.
ko.B: 내 아들아, 네 아버지의 훈계에 귀를 기울이고, \q 네 어머니의 가르침을 저버리지 마라.
ko.R: 내 아들아, 아버지가 훈계할 때 잘 들어라. \q 어머니가 가르쳐 준 것을 떠나지 마라.

decisions.choice: my son: a father teaching his son
decisions.reason: Chapters 1–9 are spoken by a father to his son, with the mother's teaching beside his (4:3–4; 31:1). Teachers in the ancient Near East also called a pupil "my son", but the mention of both parents here points to a family. The advice is for every reader.

decisions.choice: teaching: a parent's instruction
decisions.reason: The word (torah) later names God's law, but its basic sense is instruction, here given by a mother (also 6:20; 31:26).

decisions.choice: my son, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The father is speaking to his son (m1), so "my son" stays at every level. The same is true wherever the address recurs (1:10, 15).

decisions.choice: "mon fils" at every level, with no gender setting; "l'enseignement" for a parent's teaching (torah), for the whole book
decisions.reason: A father speaks to his son, so French says "mon fils", its natural address. Torah here is a mother's teaching, not the Law of Moses, so it is "l'enseignement", lowercase.

decisions.choice: "mwanangu" (my child, my son) for the father's address at every level; "mafundisho" for the teaching of father and mother
decisions.reason: "Mwanangu" is how a Swahili parent naturally calls a child, and it carries the warmth of the Hebrew address. "Mafundisho" is a parent's instruction, not the Law.

decisions.choice: hijo mío
decisions.reason: "Hijo mío" is the natural way a Spanish parent addresses a child, with the possessive after the noun; it is kept at every level and throughout Proverbs, with no gender setting, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "Hỡi con ta" (L), "Con ơi" (B, R); the father says "cha" for himself and "con" to his child
decisions.reason: "con" is the natural word a parent uses to a child, son or daughter, so no gender setting is needed, as in the English. Literal keeps "my" with "ta"; elsewhere the father speaks as "cha", the way a Vietnamese father talks to his child.

decisions.choice: "lời dạy" for the mother's teaching (torah)
decisions.reason: The word is a parent's instruction (see the meaning decision); "luật pháp" would make it a legal code.

decisions.choice: The father speaks to his son as "내 아들아", in the plain style (해라체, 너); "가르침" for the mother's torah
decisions.reason: A Korean parent speaks to a child in 해라체, and "내 아들아" is the natural address (meaning decision m1). The son is a son, so there is no gender span, as in the English. The mother's torah is her teaching (m2), not "율법" (a law code). This holds for chapters 1-11.

source.text: כִּ֤י׀לִוְיַ֤ת חֵ֓ן הֵ֬ם לְרֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲנָקִ֗ים לְגַרְגְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For a wreath of grace they [are] for your head, and necklaces for your neck.

en.L: For a wreath of grace they [are] for your head, \q and pendants for your neck.
en.B: For they will be a lovely wreath on your head \q and ornaments hanging around your neck.
en.R: Their teaching will make you honored by others, like a beautiful wreath on your head \q or a necklace around your neck.

fr.L: Car une couronne de grâce, ils [le sont] pour ta tête, \q et des colliers pour ton cou.
fr.B: Car ils seront une belle couronne sur ta tête \q et des ornements suspendus à ton cou.
fr.R: Leur enseignement te fera honorer par les autres, comme une belle couronne sur ta tête \q ou un collier autour de ton cou.

sw.L: Kwa maana hayo [ni] shada la neema kwa kichwa chako, \q na mikufu kwa shingo yako.
sw.B: Kwa maana yatakuwa shada zuri kichwani pako \q na mapambo yanayoning'inia shingoni mwako.
sw.R: Mafundisho yao yatakufanya uheshimiwe na wengine, kama shada zuri la maua kichwani pako \q au mkufu shingoni mwako.

es.L: Porque corona de gracia [serán] ellas para tu cabeza, \q y collares para tu cuello.
es.B: Porque serán una hermosa corona sobre tu cabeza \q y adornos que cuelgan de tu cuello.
es.R: Su enseñanza hará que otros te honren, como una hermosa corona en la cabeza \q o un collar en el cuello.

vi.L: Vì chúng [là] vòng hoa duyên dáng cho đầu con, \q và chuỗi ngọc cho cổ con.
vi.B: Vì chúng sẽ là vòng hoa xinh đẹp trên đầu con \q và đồ trang sức đeo quanh cổ con.
vi.R: Lời dạy của cha mẹ sẽ làm con được người khác kính trọng, như vòng hoa đẹp trên đầu con \q hay chuỗi ngọc quanh cổ con.

ko.L: 참으로 그것들은 네 머리를 위한 은혜의 화관, \q 그리고 네 목을 위한 목걸이이다.
ko.B: 그 가르침은 네 머리에 씌운 아름다운 화관, \q 네 목에 건 장식이 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그 가르침은 네가 남에게 존중받게 해 줄 것이다. 네 머리에 쓴 아름다운 화관처럼, \q 네 목에 건 목걸이처럼.

decisions.choice: wreath ... necklaces: signs of honor and favor
decisions.reason: A wreath on the head and a chain around the neck honored a person in public, as Pharaoh honored Joseph (Genesis 41:42). Proverbs 4:9 uses the same picture of wisdom.

decisions.choice: grace: beauty that wins favor
decisions.reason: The word (hen) means charm or beauty and the favor it wins from others (3:4; 3:22).

decisions.choice: will make you honored by others
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the picture means (m1) and keeps the picture as a comparison.

source.text: בְּנִ֡י אִם־יְפַתּ֥וּךָ חַ֝טָּאִ֗ים אַל־תֹּבֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: My son, if sinners entice you, do not be willing.

en.L: My son, if sinners entice you, do not be willing.
en.B: My son, if sinners try to lure you, do not go along with them.
en.R: My son, sinful people may try to get you to join them. \q Do not agree to it.

fr.L: Mon fils, si des pécheurs te séduisent, ne consens pas.
fr.B: Mon fils, si des pécheurs cherchent à t’attirer, ne les suis pas.
fr.R: Mon fils, des gens mauvais essaieront peut-être de t’entraîner avec eux. \q N’accepte pas.

sw.L: Mwanangu, wenye dhambi wakikushawishi, usikubali.
sw.B: Mwanangu, wenye dhambi wakijaribu kukuvuta, usiende pamoja nao.
sw.R: Mwanangu, watu wenye dhambi wanaweza kujaribu kukufanya ujiunge nao. \q Usikubali.

es.L: Hijo mío, si los pecadores te seducen, no consientas.
es.B: Hijo mío, si los pecadores intentan atraerte, no te dejes llevar.
es.R: Hijo mío, la gente pecadora puede tratar de que te unas a ella. \q No aceptes.

vi.L: Hỡi con ta, nếu kẻ tội lỗi dụ dỗ con, đừng ưng thuận.
vi.B: Con ơi, nếu kẻ tội lỗi tìm cách lôi kéo con, đừng nghe theo chúng.
vi.R: Con ơi, những kẻ tội lỗi có thể rủ rê con nhập bọn với chúng. \q Đừng chịu theo.

ko.L: 내 아들아, 죄인들이 너를 꾀거든 따르지 마라.
ko.B: 내 아들아, 죄인들이 너를 꾀어도 넘어가지 마라.
ko.R: 내 아들아, 죄짓는 사람들이 너를 끌어들이려 할 수도 있다. \q 그래도 따라가지 마라.

decisions.choice: entice: persuade someone gullible
decisions.reason: The verb (patah) shares its root with "the simple" (1:4, 22, 32). Sinners entice the simple, the kind of person who can be talked into anything.

decisions.choice: do not be willing: do not consent
decisions.reason: The same verb (abah) comes back in 1:25 and 1:30: those who refuse wisdom are "not willing" to have her rebuke. The son is to refuse the sinners as firmly as fools refuse wisdom.

source.text: אִם־יֹאמְרוּ֮ לְכָ֪ה אִ֫תָּ֥נוּ נֶאֶרְבָ֥ה לְדָ֑ם נִצְפְּנָ֖ה לְנָקִ֣י חִנָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: If they say, Come with us; let us lie in wait for blood; let us hide for [the] innocent without cause;

en.L: If they say, "Come with us; \q let us lie in wait for blood; \q let us lie hidden for [the] innocent without cause;
en.B: If they say, "Come with us; \q let us lie in wait to shed blood; \q let us set an ambush for the innocent, for no reason;
en.R: They may say, "Come with us! \q Let us hide and wait to kill someone. \q Let us attack an innocent person just for the fun of it.

fr.L: S’ils disent : « Viens avec nous ; \q faisons le guet pour le sang ; \q cachons-nous pour l’innocent, sans raison ;
fr.B: S’ils te disent : « Viens avec nous ; \q guettons quelqu’un pour verser son sang ; \q tendons un piège à l’innocent, sans motif ;
fr.R: Ils te diront peut-être : « Viens avec nous ! \q Cachons-nous pour attendre quelqu’un et le tuer. \q Attaquons un innocent, juste pour nous amuser.

sw.L: Wakisema, "Njoo pamoja nasi; \q tuvizie damu; \q tujifiche tumvizie asiye na hatia bila sababu;
sw.B: Wakisema, "Njoo pamoja nasi; \q tuvizie ili tumwage damu; \q tumwekee mtego asiye na hatia, bila sababu yoyote;
sw.R: Wanaweza kusema, "Njoo pamoja nasi! \q Tujifiche tumsubiri mtu tumuue. \q Tumshambulie mtu asiye na hatia kwa kujifurahisha tu.

es.L: Si dicen: «Ven con nosotros; \q acechemos para [derramar] sangre; \q escondámonos [contra el] inocente sin motivo;
es.B: Si te dicen: «Ven con nosotros; \q pongámonos al acecho para derramar sangre; \q tendamos una emboscada al inocente, sin razón alguna;
es.R: Tal vez te digan: «¡Ven con nosotros! \q Escondámonos y esperemos para matar a alguien. \q Ataquemos a una persona inocente solo por diversión.

vi.L: Nếu chúng nói: "Hãy đến với chúng tôi; \q chúng ta hãy rình rập để làm đổ máu; \q chúng ta hãy nấp chờ [người] vô tội vô cớ;
vi.B: Nếu chúng nói: "Hãy đi với chúng tôi; \q chúng ta hãy rình chờ để giết người; \q hãy phục kích người vô tội, chẳng vì lý do gì;
vi.R: Chúng có thể nói: "Hãy đi với chúng tôi! \q Chúng ta hãy nấp chờ để giết ai đó. \q Chúng ta hãy tấn công một người vô tội cho vui.

ko.L: 만일 그들이 "우리와 함께 가자. \q 피를 노리고 숨어 기다리자. \q 죄 없는 자를 까닭 없이 숨어서 노리자.
ko.B: 그들이 "우리와 함께 가자. \q 숨어서 기다리다가 피를 흘리자. \q 아무 까닭 없이 죄 없는 사람을 노려 매복하자.
ko.R: 그들은 이렇게 말할 것이다. "우리와 함께 가자! \q 숨어 기다리다가 누군가를 죽이자. \q 아무 까닭 없이 죄 없는 사람을 덮치자.

decisions.choice: without cause: modifying the ambush
alternatives: innocent without cause: someone who has done nothing to deserve it
decisions.reason: The word (hinnam) may say the ambush is for no reason, or that the victim is innocent of any wrong. Either way the attack is unprovoked. It returns in 1:17, where the net is spread "in vain".

decisions.choice: lie in wait for blood: plan to kill
decisions.reason: "Blood" stands for a life taken (1:16, 18). The gang does not hide its aim.

decisions.choice: just for the fun of it
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the gang has no cause at all; it is a stretch beyond the Hebrew, which says only "for nothing".

source.text: נִ֭בְלָעֵם כִּשְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים כְּי֣וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Let us swallow them like Sheol alive, and whole like those going down [to the] pit;

en.L: let us swallow them like Sheol, alive, \q and whole, like those going down [to the] pit;
en.B: let us gulp them down alive, as Sheol does, \q whole, like people going down into the pit;
en.R: We will swallow them up alive, the way the grave swallows the dead. \q We will take them whole, like people going down into the pit of death.

fr.L: engloutissons-les comme le Shéol, vivants, \q et entiers, comme ceux qui descendent [dans] la fosse ;
fr.B: avalons-les tout vivants, comme le fait le séjour des morts, \q tout entiers, comme ceux qui descendent dans la fosse ;
fr.R: Nous les avalerons tout vivants, comme le séjour des morts avale ceux qui meurent. \q Nous les prendrons tout entiers, comme ceux qui descendent dans le trou de la mort.

sw.L: tuwameze kama Kuzimu, wakiwa hai, \q na wakiwa kamili, kama wale washukao [katika] shimo;
sw.B: tuwameze wakiwa hai, kama Kuzimu ifanyavyo, \q wakiwa wazima, kama watu washukao shimoni;
sw.R: Tutawameza wakiwa hai, kama Kuzimu inavyowameza wafu. \q Tutawachukua wakiwa wazima, kama watu wanaoshuka katika shimo la mauti.

es.L: traguémoslos vivos como el Seol, \q y enteros, como los que descienden a [la] fosa;
es.B: devorémoslos vivos, como hace el lugar de los muertos, \q enteros, como los que bajan a la fosa;
es.R: Nos los tragaremos vivos, como el lugar de los muertos se traga a los muertos. \q Los tomaremos enteros, como a los que bajan a la fosa de la muerte.

vi.L: chúng ta hãy nuốt họ như Âm Phủ, còn sống, \q và nguyên vẹn, như những người đi xuống huyệt;
vi.B: chúng ta hãy nuốt sống họ như Âm Phủ vẫn nuốt, \q nuốt trọn, như những người đi xuống huyệt sâu;
vi.R: Chúng ta sẽ nuốt sống họ, như nơi của người chết nuốt lấy người chết. \q Chúng ta sẽ nuốt trọn họ, như những người đi xuống vực sâu của sự chết.

ko.L: 스올처럼 그들을 산 채로 삼키자. \q 구덩이로 내려가는 자들처럼 통째로 [삼키자].
ko.B: 스올이 삼키듯 그들을 산 채로 삼키고, \q 구덩이로 내려가는 사람들처럼 통째로 삼키자.
ko.R: 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳이 사람을 삼키듯 그들을 산 채로 삼켜 버리자. \q 죽음의 구덩이로 내려가는 사람들처럼 통째로 삼키자.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is where all the dead go, good and bad alike (Genesis 37:35), not a place of punishment. It is pictured as a hungry mouth that is never full (27:20; 30:15–16; Isaiah 5:14).

decisions.choice: alive and whole: like Korah and his men
decisions.reason: The earth swallowed Korah and his men and they went down alive to Sheol (Numbers 16:30–33). The gang boasts it will do the same to its victims.

decisions.choice: pit: the grave, the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The pit (bor) is a cistern or dungeon, and also, as here, a name for the grave or the underworld (Psalm 28:1; Isaiah 14:15).

decisions.choice: Sheol
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew name, since no English word means the same (m1). Readable says "the grave".

decisions.choice: "le Shéol" (Literal); "le séjour des morts" (Balanced, Readable), for the whole book
alternatives: "la tombe" at Readable, as the English Readable says "the grave"
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the name; Balanced and Readable say what it is with the usual French phrase, used for it throughout this translation. "L'enfer" would add the idea of punishment.

decisions.choice: "Kuzimu" for Sheol at every level
decisions.reason: "Kuzimu" is the Swahili word for the world of the dead, so it serves every level; the English Readable says "the grave", which in Swahili ("kaburi") would name only a single tomb.

decisions.choice: el Seol (L); el lugar de los muertos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name for the place of the dead is kept as "el Seol" at Literal, as the English keeps "Sheol"; Balanced and Readable say what it is, "el lugar de los muertos", as the terms for these books settle. "Infierno" would bring in a later idea of punishment.

decisions.choice: "Âm Phủ" (L, B); "nơi của người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (see the meaning decision). "Âm Phủ" is the word Vietnamese Bible readers know for the place of the dead, as in Psalm 139:8; a transliteration of Sheol would mean nothing to most. Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "스올" (L, B); "죽은 사람들이 있는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew name; Readable says what it is, as Psalm 139:8 does. "지옥" (hell) would add an idea of punishment the word does not have. This holds for chapters 1-11.

source.text: כָּל־ה֣וֹן יָקָ֣ר נִמְצָ֑א נְמַלֵּ֖א בָתֵּ֣ינוּ שָׁלָֽל׃

en.L: all precious wealth we will find; \q we will fill our houses [with] plunder;
en.B: we will come away with riches of every kind \q and pack our houses with what we take;
en.R: We will grab all kinds of expensive things \q and fill our houses with stolen goods.

fr.L: toute richesse précieuse nous trouverons ; \q nous remplirons nos maisons [de] butin ;
fr.B: nous ramasserons des richesses de toutes sortes \q et nous remplirons nos maisons de ce que nous aurons pris ;
fr.R: Nous prendrons toutes sortes de choses de valeur \q et nous remplirons nos maisons d’objets volés.

sw.L: kila mali ya thamani tutaipata; \q tutazijaza nyumba zetu nyara;
sw.B: tutajipatia mali za kila aina \q na kuzijaza nyumba zetu vitu tunavyoteka;
sw.R: Tutanyakua kila aina ya vitu vya thamani \q na kuzijaza nyumba zetu vitu vya wizi.

es.L: toda riqueza preciosa hallaremos; \q llenaremos nuestras casas [de] botín;
es.B: nos haremos con riquezas de toda clase \q y llenaremos nuestras casas de lo que robemos;
es.R: Agarraremos toda clase de cosas caras \q y llenaremos nuestras casas de cosas robadas.

vi.L: mọi của cải quý giá chúng ta sẽ tìm được; \q chúng ta sẽ chất đầy nhà mình [bằng] của cướp;
vi.B: chúng ta sẽ có được đủ loại của cải \q và chất đầy nhà bằng những thứ cướp được;
vi.R: Chúng ta sẽ vơ lấy đủ thứ đồ quý giá \q và chất đầy nhà bằng đồ ăn cướp.

ko.L: 온갖 귀한 재물을 우리가 얻고, \q 우리 집들을 약탈물로 채울 것이다.
ko.B: 온갖 값진 재물을 손에 넣어 \q 빼앗은 것으로 우리 집을 가득 채우자.
ko.R: 비싼 물건을 다 차지하고 \q 훔친 물건으로 우리 집을 채우자.

decisions.choice: plunder: goods taken by force
decisions.reason: The word (shalal) is the spoil of war (Judges 5:30). The gang treats robbery as a campaign.

source.text: גּ֭וֹרָ֣לְךָ תַּפִּ֣יל בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ כִּ֥יס אֶ֝חָ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your lot you will cast among us; one purse will be for all of us,

en.L: your lot you will cast among us; \q one purse will be for all of us,"
en.B: join your lot to ours; \q there will be one purse for all of us,"
en.R: Join our group, and we will all share everything we take."

fr.L: ton sort, tu le jetteras parmi nous ; \q une seule bourse sera pour nous tous »,
fr.B: unis ton sort au nôtre ; \q il y aura une seule bourse pour nous tous »,
fr.R: Viens dans notre bande, et nous partagerons tout ce que nous prendrons. »

sw.L: kura yako utaitupa kati yetu; \q mfuko mmoja utakuwa kwa sisi sote,"
sw.B: unganisha fungu lako na letu; \q kutakuwa na mfuko mmoja kwa sisi sote,"
sw.R: Jiunge na kundi letu, nasi sote tutagawana kila kitu tunachochukua."

es.L: tu suerte echarás entre nosotros; \q una sola bolsa habrá para todos nosotros»,
es.B: echa tu suerte con la nuestra; \q habrá una sola bolsa para todos»,
es.R: Únete a nuestro grupo, y entre todos repartiremos lo que saquemos».

vi.L: anh sẽ bắt thăm chung với chúng tôi; \q một túi tiền sẽ là của tất cả chúng ta."
vi.B: hãy góp phần của anh với chúng tôi; \q tất cả chúng ta sẽ chung một túi tiền."
vi.R: Hãy nhập bọn với chúng tôi, rồi tất cả chúng ta sẽ chia nhau mọi thứ lấy được."

ko.L: 너도 우리 가운데서 네 제비를 던질 것이고, \q 우리 모두에게 주머니 하나가 있을 것이다" 하거든,
ko.B: 너도 우리와 한패가 되어라. \q 우리 모두 한 주머니를 쓰자" 하고 꾀거든,
ko.R: 우리 무리에 들어와라. 빼앗은 것은 다 같이 나누자."

decisions.choice: cast your lot among us: become one of us, with an equal share
decisions.reason: Lots were cast to divide land and goods (Joshua 18:10; Psalm 22:19). To cast one's lot with a group is to join it and share in what it gets.

decisions.choice: one purse: a shared bag of takings
decisions.reason: The purse (kis) is the bag for money and weights (16:11). The offer of an equal share is the bait.

decisions.choice: the gang calls the young man "anh" and themselves "chúng tôi", with "chúng ta" for "let us"
decisions.reason: The sinners speak to him as a friend and an equal, to win him over; "anh" is the friendly word between young men. "mày" would make them openly rough, which is not how a lure sounds.

source.text: בְּנִ֗י אַל־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אִתָּ֑ם מְנַ֥ע רַ֝גְלְךָ֗ מִנְּתִיבָתָֽם׃
